speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Programme; Brieskorn links and exotic spheres
summary: The actual opening heading and programme occupy P000140: statistical mechanics, pseudodifferential operators, algebraic groups, and deformations. A report attributed to Hirzebruch then describes exotic spheres as links of isolated hypersurface singularities. The catalogue range overlaps subsequent talks; items below follow the handwritten headings. The printed exponent requires an emendation, not merely removal of an uncertainty marker.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Bass rigidity and an integral cohomology reduction
summary: P000141--P000142 report Bass’s work on rigidity of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\), relating deformations to first cohomology and proposing reduction modulo a prime. This resumes the cohomological rigidity and congruence-subgroup discussions indexed at 1964-8.1--2 and 1964-24.1--2. The established conclusion and the incompletely recorded proof reduction must be distinguished.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Anosov systems, structural stability, and Smale questions
summary: The handwritten Arnold heading is on P000142; his discussion ends on P000145. Uniform hyperbolicity, an arithmetic nilmanifold, Morse--Smale systems, Axiom A, and spectral decomposition are interspersed with explicit conjectures. Positive and negative later answers belong to different questions; in particular hyperbolicity of the nonwandering set alone does not force dense periodic points.

speaker: G. E. Shilov
title: Regular Hilbert-space functions and a first-order mean operator
summary: P000146--P000147 introduce a uniform algebra between weak and norm continuity, limiting finite-dimensional spherical means, and a mean-defined differential operator. Linear boundary problems and a fixed-point approach to a semilinear equation follow. Shilov’s 1967 papers closely match this announcement, but the operator is not the usual Hilbert-space trace Laplacian.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Uniqueness, admissibility, and viscosity for hyperbolic systems
summary: The middle and lower parts of P000147 ask when nonlinear first-order systems have unique solutions. Scalar convexity, characteristic eigenvector curves, conservation form, viscosity, and travelling waves are juxtaposed. The equations and solution classes in the hydrodynamic remarks are too incomplete for an exact publication match.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: The representation-ring completion theorem and the circle
summary: P000148 explicitly reports part of what Atiyah had explained. The augmentation-ideal completion theorem is illustrated by \(S^1\) and \(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}\). Two literal slips deserve separate treatment: calling the uncompleted map an embedding for every compact group, and giving the wrong fibre and total space for the tautological bundle.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Equivariant completion, induction, and a noncompact programme
summary: P000149--P000150 continue Atiyah’s programme: skeletal limits, equivariant vector bundles, the Borel construction, and reductions to a unitary group and maximal torus. Gelfand asks for a noncompact analogue and suggests a Plancherel replacement for dimension, but does not specify a representation ring or ideal. The family-index explanation is continued at record 104.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Canonical ensembles and factorial correlation functions
summary: The first lecture starts at P000151 and ends near the top of P000155. It defines continuum and lattice models, the thermodynamic limit, canonical Gibbs weights, and correlation densities. The 1968 lectures explicitly identify the autumn 1966 Gelfand seminar as a source, while tracing the earlier course to Khumsan in September 1965. Much of this first lecture is foundational exposition, not a new result. The ordered-pair convention is retained consistently.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Bulk correlations, clustering, and representative means
summary: The second lecture begins midway down P000155 and ends on P000157. It deliberately labels several thermodynamic assertions as hypotheses, allows an effective specific volume depending on the correlation order, and uses clustering to argue that pair observables concentrate. The 1968 version restores an integrable decay requirement; nevertheless the displayed variance proof needs more than the stated \(L^1\) condition on the pair kernel. Our bounded development isolates the exact probabilistic implication and its limits.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Isolation of the trivial representation and lattice finiteness
summary: Two finiteness conclusions for lattices are announced on P000158, followed by the representation-theoretic mechanism now called property \(T\). Kazhdan’s short paper, received two weeks after the seminar, is an unusually close match. A separate sentence about groups over \(\mathbb Q\) retains no conclusion and cannot be identified with a theorem.

speaker: Lee Lorch
title: Higher monotonicity of zeros and wave integrals
summary: The lecturer’s handwritten name on P000158 is uncertain; the MCCME entry and the joint work with Peter Szego identify Lee Lorch. The page treats Sturm comparison, higher finite differences of zeros, Bessel and Airy examples, and integrals between consecutive zeros. The strict inequality cannot follow from the weak derivative hypotheses exactly as written. Gelfand’s endpoint remark is mathematically suggestive but not completely recorded.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A recapitulation of equivariant K-theory and completion
summary: On P000159 Gelfand explicitly repeats Bernstein’s and Atiyah’s material: equivariant bundles, the Borel construction, the representation-ring action, and the approximate identification with ordinary K-theory. These are new notebook occurrences of the same constructions, not additional discovery claims.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Families of elliptic operators and the index bundle
summary: P000159--P000160 supply the analytic construction behind the K-theoretic direct image, then a finite-dimensional modification of a Fredholm family. The essential issue is that kernel dimensions jump. The index is a virtual bundle after stabilization, not generally the difference of two pre-existing kernel and cokernel bundles. This continues 1964-15.4.
